Subject (in full) Press Report regarding rice stored on unoccupied
bank premises on Honan Road.

Made by and Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

With reference to the attached translation
of extract from the Lieh Pao of March 23, 1940,
regarding rice being stored in the former premises
of Agricultural Bank, Honan Road, enquiries show
that this address is 515 Honan Road, and is to be
occupied by a new bank called Woo Ming Bank (滬民銀行),
sponsored by the Kiangsu-Chekiang-Anhwei Revenue
Bureau, 230 Kiukiang Road.

On March 22, approximately 1,000 bags of
rice were removed to this place under the escort of
three Japanese in civilian clothes and are at present
stored there guarded by men belonging to the Revenue
Bureau.

D. I.

D.C. (Special Branch)

参照所附1940年3月23日《力报》摘录译文，

储存有大米，经查询，该地址为河南路515号，

Lich Pao ( 力報 ) of March 23 rd, 1940.
RICE BEING STORLD IN AN UNOCCUPIED BANK
At about noon last Thursday as I was walking
along Honan Road, I noticed a number of coolies engaged

Made by __________ and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao Liang

Zau Sih Chun(邵式軍), mentioned in
attached applications, is a relative of the Cheng Tung
Lao family. Being an old employee of the Consolidated
Tax Bureau he was recommended to the present post by
one Li Han Ching (李漢青) whose antecedents were
reported on previously. Taking advantage of the
unsettled situation in Shanghai when he took charge
Zau, it is reported, made an agreement with the
Japanese authorities to which he was entitled to a
commission for the collection of revenue and through
this has made a large fortune. The other financial
organizations which were formed later like the Salt
and Saltpetre offices, have been working on a "pay"
system, i.e. they have turned all proceeds to the
Japanese besides defraying their own expenses.
An attempt was made on the life of Zau on October 17,
1938, when he was travelling on Jessfield Road in an
armoured car.

There appear to be no objection to the
transfer of the attendants' licences subject to a test
being given in the use of guns.

Zau himself is also applying for a licence
to carry firearms. It is reported that he is a heavy
opium smoker and is not physically fit to carry
firearms. I also suggest that he be subject to a test
in the use of a pistol before he is given a licence.

Happy to know that you have been promoted

wish to thank for your work to all Shanghai community,
and to offer you with one information of great importance

Do you know why your recent promotion is
very much disliked by Japanese people? The causes and
effects we now wish to unveil.

We know your No. 1 detective Shih Chi
Liang has through various unjust means squeezed immense
money deposited in foreign banks. He can use such ways

Shih is known outside as his "adopted son", and is used

former superior official are hated by him, he openly
expressed recently on a friend's banquet. He has also
close connections with Japanese Consulate , Reform
Government and all Wang Ching wei figures, no wonder
you are disliked. This is only his primary efforts; you
will see major ones later.

This information must keep secretly for your
good self.

尊敬的先生：

欣闻您已晋升为上海公共租界工部局政治部主任。我们一直钦佩您的公正无私。因此向您祝贺，感谢您为上海各界所做的工作，并向您提供一条对您至关重要的信息。

您知道为什么您的近期晋升非常不受日本人待见吗？我们现在希望揭示其原因和后果。

我们知道您的头号侦探施志良通过各种不公正手段，榨取了大量存入外国银行的资金。他之所以能使用这些手段，是因为他的前上司与他关系极为亲密，施在外面被称为其“干儿子”，并且习惯于奉承所有外籍警官。

他对您的晋升及其前任上级官员的调任有多么憎恨，他最近在朋友的宴会上公开表达了这一点。他还与日本领事馆、维新政府以及所有汪精卫派人物有着密切联系，难怪您不受欢迎。这仅仅是他的初步行动；您稍后将看到更大的动作。

此信息请务必为您个人保密。

BRANCHES OF CONSOLIDATED TAX BUREAU BEING SUPPRESSED

In connection with the establishment of branches by the Kiangsu-Chekiang-Anhwei Consolidated Tax Bureau for the collection of wine and tobacco taxes in Kiangsu Province, the Kiangsu Provincial Government has now been instructed by the Executive Yuan of the "Reformed Government" to prohibit such establishments. Consequently, the Soochow Police Bureau, of which Tung Yeu-yen (董支賢) is the Commissioner, has been instructed to order the removal of the signboard of the Soochow Branch of the Consolidated Tax Bureau. The various Hsiens in Kiangsu Province have been notified accordingly by the Finance Department of the Kiangsu Provincial Government.

As a branch of the Consolidated Tax Bureau is also in existence in Wusih, the Wusih Police Bureau has been instructed to order the removal of its signboard. The branches of the Tax Bureau at Wusih, Changchow and Kiangyin will also be removed. Merchants have also been informed not to pay consolidated taxes to any of the branches of the Bureau.

and native wine. This agreement, in theory, is
still in force after the withdrawal of the
